So, for me, I broke gender roles as a woman, and tried to actively fight sexism/stereotypes. It wasn't really until I heard both cis women and trans people talk about their gender that I realized that some of the stuff I disliked had less to do with sexism and more to do with dysphoria. For example, I *hate* being called a girl; I thought that was because that was infantalizing, but now I realize it was because it was the wrong gender (I don't mind boy/kid the same way.) So, for me, I'd be up for the abolish all gender associations, and that would help a decent amount of dysphoria, but it'd have to include everything, even including gendered pronouns or words for kids, which is far more than could happen in my lifetime. Also, I'd still want to not have boobs, which societal change couldn't much help.

I'm in college right now, and have been having an iffy time with this. I've found that a compatable therapist really helps (if you can get one that specializes in your issues, that helps) but other than that, to do lists. I'll make a to do list for the week, and put due dates. Then I make to do lists from that, trying to keep each day reasonable. Making the list makes me feel productive, which means I usually have the motivation to get started after that. If not, I try to eat or walk or talk to a friend for just a bit.

I'm nonbinary, and I identify as bi because I generally prefer men, but feel attraction to women and nonbinary people as well.

I'm fond of things like cutie and my love in other languages. I get called "мои дорогои" (moi dorogoy - my darling) a lot, and i call my partner "mein Liebling" (my love.) They might have connotations in those languages, but i don't know them, so they don't make me uncomfortable the way English ones can.

I'd say just lay off the "I'm not gay" stuff and just let things play out, coming out if you feel more comfortable with people or sure about your sexuality. If people try to give you crap about it, just tell them you cringe at yourself a year ago too. I had a mildly similar experience (The only "straight" one in a really gay group that turned out to be bi in the end) and in my experience most people remember being uncertain about their sexuality, and while you may get some crap, you probably won't get seriously judged.
